header.title: Curse tablets from Africa Proconsularis (Epigraphic Database Heidelberg): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Latin curse tablets
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:defix:edh:africa-proconsularis:lat, from the Epigraphic Database Heidelberg (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit the Epigraphic Database Heidelberg and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

notes.47991.1.1: 47991: 'Hos' and 'ritine' are marked as irregular forms and are taken, doubtfully, as for haec and retine ('keep'); the first line is obscure, and Patelaria Minor is read as a personal name. 'Bictor' and 'bidere' are Victor and videre. *instrumentarius*, broken over three lines, is a trade or office of uncertain sense (perhaps an instrument-maker or a keeper of records), left in Latin. In 3.5 the database gives one word three ways (hos, ho⟨s⟩, and OC as written); translated 'these'. 'AEE' is a letter string, kept as it stands. 50483 and 50484 name people by their mothers; in 50484 the mother's name is lost. 67821.1.4: the tablet has VET, read as vel ('or'). 67821.2 is in Greek letters, magical words and single letters, transliterated and not translated; its last line has erased letters ([[..]]) and a loss, and 'tutt' is unclear.

nodes.text: Donatus to your [people]: this we wish for you,
